```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Query Azure Database for PostgreSQL with a visitor's Microsoft account.
The app uses RPostgres and DBI, so you can use the same queries and dbplyr
code as with other PostgreSQL connections.

## Enable Entra access

Install `RPostgres`. Your administrator must
[enable Entra authentication and provision database roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/security/security-entra-configure)
for the users or groups who will use the app. Obtain the database role name
and a CA bundle trusted by the server.

Create an Entra Web app registration for PostgreSQL access with
`http://localhost:8100` as the redirect URI. The `services = "postgres"`
preset below requests the PostgreSQL token.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "postgres",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_azure_postgres(
    auth$connection,
    host = "example.postgres.database.azure.com",
    dbname = "reporting",
    user = "reporting-readers",
    sslrootcert = "path/to/root-ca.pem"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

Replace `user` with the database role provisioned for the visitor or their
group. The example uses a shared group role; the database verifies the
signed-in person's membership. Set `sslrootcert` to your CA bundle path.
You can omit it if libpq already has the correct bundle configured.

## Read a table

Replace the identity query with SQL against your data, for example:

```{r table-query}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM reporting.orders LIMIT 20")
})
```

For dbplyr, pass `connection` to `dplyr::tbl()`. Use DBI parameter binding
for SQL values entered by visitors.

## Connection options

The helper uses `dbname` for the database name, following RPostgres.
Options such as `port` and `connect_timeout` go to RPostgres; see
`?oauth_db_azure_postgres`.

Create `con` inside `server()` and call it before each operation. The helper
reuses connections and closes them on account changes, sign-out, or session
end. For custom login settings or cached data, see
[Authentication and sessions](authorization.html).
